learning: Iteration 7 (track 0.09, row ±0.07) collapsed the oval to 0.15 and cut the s-bend to 0.18, while removing slalom line losses. This race tests whether the ±0.07 row is compatible with the 0.10 m track. If the oval holds, the row is confirmed and the s-bend turn rate is the next lever.
notes: Geometry follows the Builder's iteration 8 proposal (track 0.10 m, row ±0.07 m, 12 mm footprint). Controller is iteration 5's best values, unchanged. All ten measurements are requested so the oval, s-bend and slalom effects can be separated.
rationale: Iteration 7 changed two geometry variables at once (wheel_track 0.10 to 0.09 m and row x=±0.06 to ±0.07). Its oval finish fell from 20/20 to 3/20 and s-bend progress fell from 0.42 to 0.18, while slalom line losses fell from 1.0 to 0.0. Iteration 4 showed that extra controller authority also lowers the oval finish rate, so the narrower track is the likely cause of the oval collapse. Iteration 5 (track 0.10, row ±0.06) gave 20/20 oval finishes and the best s-bend progress (0.42). Iteration 6 showed a 0.016 footprint cuts the oval to 0.55 without fixing the slalom, so footprint is rejected. I accept the Builder's iteration 8 geometry: wheel_track back to 0.10 m, the row widened to x=±0.07 at y=0.08, and 12 mm footprints. This isolates whether the wider row alone keeps the oval stable while removing the slalom line losses. The controller is iteration 5's best set, unchanged, because the row change keeps the same five sensor weights. Expected: oval finish at least 0.85, slalom line losses near 0 with progress above 0.12, and s-bend progress at or above 0.42. The main risk is that the wider row alone destabilises the oval, which the next race will show.
